aetosauroides:research:1.title: 2026 in archosaur paleontology (research: General pseudosuchian research)

facts.statement: The genus Aetosauroides was described by Casamiquela in 1960.
Aetosauroides is one of four known aetosaur genera from South America.
facts.quote: It is one of four aetosaurs known from South America

facts.statement: Fossils of Aetosauroides have been found in northwestern Argentina and southeastern Brazil.
facts.quote: Fossils have been found in the Cancha de Bochas Member of the Ischigualasto Formation in the Ischigualasto-Villa Unión Basin in northwestern Argentina and the Santa Maria Formation in the Paraná Basin in southeastern Brazil.

facts.statement: Most Aetosauroides individuals measured around 1.3 meters in length, though one large individual reached 2.4 meters.
facts.quote: Most individuals of Aetosauroides measured around 1.3 m in length, with one large individual reaching 2.4 m

facts.statement: Histological analysis of a large Aetosauroides specimen suggests it reached an age of 23 years.
facts.quote: with histology suggesting an age of 23 years

facts.statement: The premaxilla of A. scagliai had a shovel-shaped tip that lacked the prominent lateral expansion seen in desmatosuchines.
facts.quote: The premaxilla's shovel-shaped tip in A. scagliai lacked the same prominence as the lateral expansion found in desmatosuchines.

facts.statement: Aetosauroides was proposed to be synonymous with the genus Stagonolepis in 1996 and 2002, but this synonymy is not accepted.
facts.quote: Aetosauroides was proposed to be synonymous with the genus Stagonolepis in 1996 and 2002.

facts.statement: A 2012 phylogenetic analysis found that Aetosauroides lies outside the family Stagonolepididae.
facts.quote: A phylogenetic analysis presented by Julia B. Desojo, Martin D. Ezcurra and Edio E. Kischlat in 2012 found that Aetosauroides lies outside Stagonolepididae.

facts.statement: Despite having carnivore-like teeth, A. scagliai's shovel-shaped snout and toothless jaw tips suggest it was an omnivore.
facts.quote: Although A. scagliai had recurved ziphodont teeth typical of carnivores, its shovel-shaped snout and its edentulous anterior premaxilla and dentary suggest that it was omnivorous.

facts.statement: A pathological specimen of A. scagliai shows bone indicative of periostitis, believed to be caused by non-traumatic stress followed by a pyogenic infection.
facts.quote: This palaeopathology is believed to have been caused by some sort of non-traumatic stress followed by a pyogenic infection.

facts.statement: The time range for Aetosauroides is estimated from 237 to 227.3 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Carnian to Carnian (237 to 227.3 million years ago)

facts.statement: Researchers have suggested that sexual dimorphism exists in Aetosauroides, with males potentially reaching 2 meters in length.
facts.quote: Sexual dimorphism has been suggested for Aetosauroides, with males reaching the 2 m size range.

facts.statement: A 2011 study proposed that the species A. subsulcatus and A. inhamandensis are synonymous with the type species A. scagliai.
facts.quote: In a 2011 study, A. subsulcatus and A. inhamandensis were proposed to be synonymous with A. scagliai.

facts.statement: Two 2021 studies proposed that Polesinesuchus aurelioi is a junior synonym of Aetosauroides based on similarities in juvenile vertebrae and braincase structures.
facts.quote: Additionally, a contemporary aetosaur named from a juvenile specimen in 2014, Polesinesuchus aurelioi, was found to be similar in its vertebrae and the basioccipital of its braincase to juvenile specimens of Aetosauroides in two 2021 studies, and it was proposed as a junior synonym of the latter.

rejected.statement: Aetosauroides lived during the late Carnian and early Norian stages, making it one of the oldest known aetosaurs.
rejected.quote: The strata date to the late Carnian and early Norian stages, making Aetosauroides one of the oldest aetosaurs.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'the late Carnian and early Norian stages making'

rejected.statement: Aetosauroides is distinguished from Stagonolepis by features such as maxillae that do not touch the nostrils, oval-shaped holes on vertebral centra, and a convex lower jaw margin.
rejected.quote: Among these are maxillae that do not touch the nostrils, oval-shaped holes on the centra of the vertebrae, and a convex margin of the lower jaw.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'maxillae that do not touch the nostrils oval-shaped'

rejected.statement: If the 2012 phylogeny is correct, Aetosauroides would be the first known aetosaur that is not a stagonolepidid.
rejected.quote: If this phylogeny is correct, Stagonolepididae and Aetosauria would not be equivalent groupings, and Aetosauroides would be the first non-stagonolepidid aetosaur.
